entry.title: SCUBA Lab gets $200,000 NSF ERI Funding to Build Multi-Robot Test-bed!

link.title: SCUBA Lab gets $200,000 NSF ERI Funding to Build Multi-Robot Test-bed!

entry.content:
We’ve got some exciting news from the lab today!

SCUBA Lab at the College of Engineering and Computer Science at Florida Atlantic University has secured a $200,000 grant from the National Science Foundation (NSF) to develop an innovative testbed to transform how autonomous aerial robots coordinate in real-world environments.

Led by Dr. Pratik Mukherjee, this groundbreaking project combines advanced research, hands-on student learning, and nationwide collaboration, paving the way for resilient, scalable robot systems.

Learn how we’re shaping the future of autonomous robotics: FAU Announcement and NSF Award Page

entry.title: SCUBA Lab Roboticists won the best paper at the 38th Florida Conference on Recent Advances in Robotics (FCRAR)!

link.title: SCUBA Lab Roboticists won the best paper at the 38th Florida Conference on Recent Advances in Robotics (FCRAR)!

entry.content: Taiwo Hazeez, Cosme Penney and Daniel Guido’s paper titled “Evaluating Relative Localization in GPS-Denied Environments Using Starling2 UAVs” won the best paper award!

entry.title: SCUBA Lab has a strong presence at the 38th Florida Conference on Recent Advances in Robotics (FCRAR)!

link.title: SCUBA Lab has a strong presence at the 38th Florida Conference on Recent Advances in Robotics (FCRAR)!

entry.content:
Taiwo Hazeez, Cosme Penney and Daniel Guido had their paper titled “Evaluating Relative Localization in GPS-Denied Environments Using Starling2 UAVs” accepted!

Daniel Granda, Vladimir Gunichev and Caleb Sanchez had their paper titled “ Accelerating Early-Stage Robot Navigation Development with Motion Capture and ROS” accepted!

Caleb Sanchez had his abstract “Revealing All the Mysteries of Using Motion Capture System for Robot Localization” accepted!

Congrats to all the SCUBA roboticists!
